This post also interests me. I have been pondering getting into welding as a builder hobby type of thing. From some of my limited research (and working with some welders over the years), I think I want a DC stick machine that can handle a variety of sticks that are out there? A good cut off saw (bandsaw and portable bandsaw). Good angle grinder. Clamps, more clamps and then some additional clamps. I guess my question is what am I missing and if I wanted to get into other than just regular steel welding what do I need for more difficult welding like aluminum.
A tig torch for aluminum (fuck push pull guns or spool guns), but you’ll want a stick machine that can do AC for that.

As a hobby welder, my advice would be to stay away from any type of autofeed welders. They have the gas on the spool of wire and imo it creates an ugly weld. Mig stick welders are amazing for any type of mild steel and even some high carbon projects( welding billets together to make damascus knifes) tig is for aluminum welding and again stick with a nice heavy duty stick application. The best welder I've used was a Miller thunderbolt 225. Key word is " ive used". There are plenty of good ones out there but they can be quite pricey if all your looking to do is hobby stuff. Another good thing to invest in is a good helmet. Don't cheap out on that. They have ones that you can see through and as soon as the arc happens it switches over so that you don't go blind. There is a lot more information on the web that will give all of the basics on start any welding project. And as another person said STAY VENTILATED!!!

Ask a hundred welders how to weld something, you’ll get a hundred different answers. Forehand solid and metal core wires. Backhand flux core and stick. I would not recommend gasless fluxcore unless you’re desperate. Don’t cross contaminate carbon and stainless steels. This means welding them together or using grinding wheels/consumables on both. When welding SS, wire or filler metal can always be better but not inferior to the base metal. IE when welding 308 stainless you can use 308, 316, 316L, but not 304. In a situation where you DO want to weld carbon to stainless, use 309 filler metal. ALWAYS MAKE SURE YOUR GAS IS ON BEFORE STRIKING AN ARC.
